general_information.Description: -Objective: To provide the basic knowledge about the berverage industry as well as the knowledge of the world beverage culture in operating the Restaurant - Bar. -Description: This course is the continued part of RES213. This course focus on the beverage service of the Hospitality Industry including spirits, wines, beers and mixology beverages. Topics include purchasing, resource control, beverage storage and issuing, bar stocks and sales control, bar customer care, safety and security, managing bar wastage, the law and sale of liquor. -Teaching method: lecture, discussion, demonstration, project based learning, group work
general_information.StudentTasks: - Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend more than 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose - Read the textbook in advance - Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

description: -Objective: To provide the basic knowledge about the berverage industry as well as the knowledge of the world beverage culture in operating the Restaurant - Bar. -Description: This course is the continued part of RES213. This course focus on the beverage service of the Hospitality Industry including spirits, wines, beers and mixology beverages. Topics include purchasing, resource control, beverage storage and issuing, bar stocks and sales control, bar customer care, safety and security, managing bar wastage, the law and sale of liquor. -Teaching method: lecture, discussion, demonstration, project based learning, group work

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Manage and correctly arrange sanitation standards and routines for the bar setup.
Explain the Stirring, Shaking, Blending, and Building methods of drink mixing.
Identify and outline the types of jobs in the beverage industry.
Identify the functions and relations of the purchase order, the invoice, and the credit memo.
Identify the needs of targeting a clientele.
Create and use a workable business plan for a bar.
Present basic knowledge about tea and coffee beverages

assessments.Question Type: Each student shoud make at least 1 individual presentation, case analysis during the course in front of the class. Topics will be varied based on the topics in the textbook.
assessments.Note: Participation grade will be given based on students' preparation, and quantity as well as quality of participation in classroom; quality of participation is demonstrated through asking relevant questions, making statements that add to and facilitate class discussion, and builds upon others’ comments. Class preparation and pre-reading before lecture will be assessed upon individuals' understanding and ability to answer questions in the class. Individuals will be called up randomly to be assessed.

assessments.CLO: CLO1, CLO2, CLO3, CLO4, CLO5, CLO6, CLO7, CLO8
assessments.Question Type: Four or five students per group. Groups and groups ideas are determined on the third session of the course. Work will be break down into stages and examined during the course. Final work to be submitted prior to the presentation of the topic.
assessments.No Question: Minimum length of the group assignment should be 10 pages, excluding appendices
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Based on topics of studied units
assessments.Note: All assignments should be typed and double-spaced with 13-point font, and must be submitted in soft copy. A deduction of 10% of the assignment mark will be applied for each day of late submission Evaluation will be based on both presentation and written report (reccommded 30%, 70% accordingly)

assessments.CLO: CLO1, CLO2, CLO3, CLO4, CLO5, CLO6, CLO7
assessments.Question Type: Multiple choice, exercises or essay questions
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Quizzes will test for knowledge of subjects in the chapter assigned for that day.
assessments.Note: These quizzes will be given at various times during class (beginning, middle or end). Total number of quizzes: 2
